title: Atlas for Government: The Only FedRAMP® Class D Certified Cross-Cloud Operational Database
summary: MongoDB Atlas for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) certification and adds Azure support. Run multi-cloud workloads securely. Get started today.
body_markdown:
Federal, state, and local agencies are under mounting pressure to modernize legacy systems, adopt AI, and protect sensitive data, all at the same time. Many of the databases that can currently handle an agency's most sensitive, high-impact workloads are native to a single cloud and run nowhere else, leaving agencies with a limited set of authorized options and little room to change course when missions, mandates, or threats shift.


MongoDB is the intelligent data platform for the AI era, and today we're extending it to the workloads where the stakes are highest: MongoDB Atlas for Government has achieved FedRAMP® Class D Certification. Formerly known as FedRAMP High, Class D is the highest level of assessment under the Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP). Atlas for Government has also added support for Azure Government, expanding its existing support for AWS GovCloud and Commercial Regions and Google Cloud Assured Workloads.


Together, these milestones make MongoDB Atlas for Government the only FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified cross-cloud operational database in the world. Public sector organizations and the independent software vendors (ISVs) that serve them can now run their most sensitive mission-critical workloads—including production AI applications built on real-time operational data—on a single platform and on the cloud provider of their choice, across AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud. To learn more, visit the[MongoDB Atlas for Government product page](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/atlas-for-government) or the[FedRAMP Marketplace page](https://www.fedramp.gov/marketplace/products/FR2122150307/) .


## What is MongoDB Atlas for Government?


MongoDB Atlas for Government is an independent, dedicated environment of the MongoDB Atlas intelligent data platform built specifically for the U.S. public sector and the ISVs that build government solutions. It brings the core capabilities of MongoDB’s[intelligent data platform](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform) to government, giving agencies a fully managed way to deploy, run, and scale mission-critical applications in the cloud, including transactional workloads, search, vector search for AI applications, and time series data, all within a single, unified data platform.


Atlas for Government is operated by MongoDB employees who are United States persons on U.S. soil, and all encryption within MongoDB-managed infrastructure is FIPS 140-3 validated. The platform maintains a 99.995% uptime SLA and has been generally available since 2021.


MongoDB Atlas for Government is already trusted across the federal government. MongoDB works with 13 U.S. Federal Cabinet-level agencies. With FedRAMP Class D (High) certification, agencies like these can bring even more sensitive, high-impact workloads to Atlas for Government. For example, a health agency could modernize benefits and eligibility systems that handle protected health information and personally identifiable information. A financial agency could run real-time fraud detection across high-volume transaction streams. And a civilian agency could build an AI application that lets analysts search policy and case records in natural language, without that data leaving a FedRAMP Class D (High) environment.


## What is FedRAMP Class D (High)?


FedRAMP provides the standardized authorization framework that cloud service providers (CSPs) must successfully navigate to demonstrate compliance with federal security requirements before hosting federal agency workloads. In 2026, FedRAMP moved away from labeling these standards Low, Moderate, and High, replacing them with a four-tier Certification Class system, A through D. FedRAMP Class D (High) is the direct successor to what was previously known as FedRAMP High, and it remains the most rigorous tier a CSP can achieve within the FedRAMP program.


FedRAMP Class D (High) certification is designed for cloud services that support an agency's high-impact systems, where a security failure could have severe or catastrophic consequences for operations, assets, or people. This includes systems tied to national security, law enforcement, and emergency response, as well as high-impact modernization initiatives across civilian agencies. Achieving this certification requires meeting hundreds of stringent security controls covering everything from access management to incident response.


MongoDB Atlas for Government achieved FedRAMP Moderate authorization in 2023 and has been a trusted, fully managed data platform for federal agencies and ISVs since then. With FedRAMP Class D (High) certification, that foundation is now extended to high-impact workloads, including production AI applications. Agencies can bring those workloads to the cloud on a platform that meets the security and compliance requirements for high-impact systems, and build secure, production-grade AI applications on top of them.


## Freedom to run anywhere: Now spanning AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud


With the addition of support for Azure Government, MongoDB Atlas for Government now runs across all three major cloud providers: AWS (both GovCloud and AWS commercial regions), Google Cloud (via Assured Workloads), and Azure Government. This makes MongoDB Atlas for Government the only FedRAMP Class D (High) certified, cross-cloud database in the world.


For public sector organizations, this cross-cloud support is about more than convenience. A database tied to a single cloud provider limits an agency's options if costs rise, a mission requirement changes, or a new mandate calls for a different cloud environment. MongoDB Atlas for Government gives agencies and ISVs the freedom to run their workloads on the cloud that best fits their needs today, and to change that decision later without rewriting their applications. Within FedRAMP-certified cloud environments (AWS GovCloud, Google Cloud Assured Workloads, and Azure Government), data can be distributed across providers to optimize for performance, cost, or resilience, and to strengthen disaster recovery with automatic failover across providers.


Getting started on Azure Government works the same way as it does on AWS GovCloud or Google Cloud Assured Workloads. Agencies and ISVs can create a project in Atlas for Government, designate it as a FedRAMP Class D (High) Gov Regions Only project, and select Azure as the cloud provider when creating a cluster.


## Protecting data and powering AI at the highest level


FedRAMP Class D (High) sets a high bar for how a provider documents, assesses, and maintains its security program, but that is only one part of the picture. Agencies handling the country's most sensitive data also need assurance that the data itself stays protected, even if a system is compromised.


MongoDB Atlas for Government provides robust protection for sensitive data, supporting workloads that include Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Protected Health Information (PHI), and Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) data. Data at rest is protected using database encryption with Customer Managed Keys, and data in transit is protected via TLS.


For organizations that require protection beyond the authorization boundary,[MongoDB Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/) performs encryption and decryption client-side, so designated fields remain encrypted throughout their lifecycle, in transit, at rest, and in use. MongoDB, cloud operators, and even the organization's own database administrators never have access to keys or unencrypted data.


This same secure foundation enables agencies to deploy production AI applications in their high-impact environments. MongoDB Atlas for Government includes MongoDB Vector Search, allowing teams to build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and other AI-powered applications directly on top of their operational data. Instead of standing up a separate vector database and building a pipeline to keep it in sync, agencies can run transactional workloads, search, and vector search in a single, FedRAMP Class D-certified environment, reducing both complexity and risk.


## How to get started with MongoDB Atlas for Government


With FedRAMP Class D (High) certification and support for Azure Government, MongoDB’s intelligent data platform for the AI era now reaches the public sector’s highest-stakes missions. MongoDB Atlas for Government gives public sector organizations and ISVs a secure, fully managed, and truly multi-cloud way to run their most sensitive workloads and build production AI applications.


To get started, visit the[MongoDB Atlas for Government](https://www.mongodb.com/products/platform/atlas-for-government) product page, view the[FedRAMP Marketplace](https://marketplace.fedramp.gov/) listing, or refer to the[Atlas for Government documentation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/government/) for setup details.


## FAQ


**What is MongoDB Atlas for Government?**


MongoDB Atlas for Government is an independent, dedicated environment of MongoDB Atlas built for the U.S. public sector and the ISVs that build government solutions. It is a fully managed, FedRAMP Class D (High) certified operational database.


**What is FedRAMP Class D (High)?**


FedRAMP Class D (High) is the highest tier in FedRAMP’s four-tier Certification Class system and the direct successor to what was previously known as FedRAMP High. It is designed for cloud services that support high-impact government systems.


**Which cloud providers does Atlas for Government support?**


Atlas for Government runs on AWS (GovCloud and Commercial Regions), Google Cloud (via Assured Workloads), and Azure Government. Within FedRAMP-certified cloud environments, data can be distributed across providers with automatic failover.


**Can agencies build AI applications on Atlas for Government?**


Yes. MongoDB Vector Search enables teams to build retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and other AI applications directly on operational data, in a single FedRAMP Class D (High) certified environment, without a separate vector database or sync pipeline.
